summary: Midflight worker migration causes heartbeat frames to interleave and suppress concluding sentence on SSE streams
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaDocs, dedicated tenant) reports repeated SSE streaming requests where the response completes server-side but the client never receives the natural concluding sentence. Instead the stream contains a burst of heartbeat events that arrive interleaved with the last content fragments; the client parser treats the heartbeat burst as a terminal boundary and drops the final sentence.

Impact:
- Several dozen production requests over the last 24h returned partial documents (missing final sentence/closing punctuation).
- Causes downstream document-merging pipeline to produce incomplete artifacts for NovaDocs customers.
- Customer reports loss of user-facing content; elevated to P1 due to customer SLA and business impact.

Environment:
- Redwood prod region: us-west-2 (customer-dedicated pool).
- Model: gpt-4o-mini, pinned variant v2026-03-05.
- Dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling; observed worker node reassignments during reported windows.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) POST /v1/stream with SSE to the NovaDocs tenant endpoint with a ~1200-token prompt that elicits a 5-8 sentence paragraph.
2) Keep client SSE connection open and allow streaming to finish naturally.
3) Observe stream: final sentence missing and final SSE events include several heartbeat JSON objects before connection close.

Observed behavior:
- Server-side logs indicate inference completed and terminal token emitted; however the client stream shows heartbeat frames (type: keepalive) arriving mixed with last content fragments. The client SDK's SSE parser closes the message boundary prematurely and final content is never appended.

Expected behavior:
- Heartbeat/keepalive frames should not interleave with terminal content fragments. If they do, they must be clearly delimited and the client should be able to reassemble the concluding sentence.

Temporary workaround (customer):
- NovaDocs temporarily switched their frontend SSE parser to ignore keepalive events until an explicit end-of-message marker is received. This restores behavior for them but is fragile across SDKs.

Logs / Traces / IDs:
- Example trace ID (customer request): 8f3d2a7b-prod-usw2-001
- Worker migration window: 2026-03-09T18:22:00Z to 2026-03-09T18:25:00Z
- Backend node IDs: gpu-pool-24a -> gpu-pool-24b (migration logged by scheduler).

Investigation notes:
- SRE snapshot shows scheduler initiated ephemeral migration for capacity smoothing; the runtime gracefully forwarded active KV cache to the new worker but did not quiesce keepalive logic during handoff.
- Inferred timeline: new worker accepted requests and replayed a short sequence of keepalive frames intended for session health checks; those frames were emitted while the final content fragments (terminal tokens) were still being flushed from the original worker.
- Client SDKs treat keepalive frames uniformly as non-content SSE events, but our server implementation currently emits keepalives with the same event semantics and without an explicit "sequence" envelope. When interleaved, some client-side parsers conflate the keepalive and the final content boundary.
- Similar but distinct from previously reported resume/offset issues: here the content existed and was emitted, but arrival ordering placed keepalives between the last text fragments.

Repro rate:
- Reproduced against a test dedicated pool by running synthetic load while triggering a planned worker reassign. Reproducible ~70% under the same timing pattern.

Next steps / proposed fixes:
1) Short-term: adjust server-side keepalive behavior so that keepalive frames are suppressed during the final-content flush window (implementation toggle: suppress-keepalive-during-terminal-flush).
2) Medium-term: introduce explicit sequencing metadata for SSE events (e.g., event_seq, final=true) so clients can reassemble deterministically even if arrival is out of order.
3) Update SDKs to: a) treat keepalive events as ignorable for boundary detection, b) prefer server-provided final flag when present.
4) Add scheduler quiesce step: when migrating an active stream, signal runtime to hold keepalive emissions until terminal flush completes.

Owner(s): Marco Duarte (SRE/serving-runtime) for immediate mitigation; Elena Park (Support) to coordinate with NovaDocs and confirm customer-side fix.

2026-03-10 15:20 - NovaDocs (Customer): After client-side ignore-keepalive change, partials stopped for immediate tests; request a durable server-side fix and timeline.

2026-03-11 07:48 - Marco Duarte (SRE): Short-term toggle implemented on staging: suppress-keepalive-during-terminal-flush=true. Verified synthetic repro is blocked; no interleaved keepalives seen in test runs. Opening PR for regulated rollout.

resolution_notes: Staging toggle implemented and verified (suppress keepalive during final flush). PR created for runtime: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1842. Scheduler quiesce change drafted (INT task). Customer will validate post-canary. Long-term work (sequence metadata + SDK updates) scheduled as product backlog items.
final_verdict: Pending prod rollout and customer validation
